INTRODUCTIONM
In this lesson you will learn about the dangers and safety practices necessary while working in and around an aircraft flight line or otherwise called the Ramp.
The hazards associated with aircraft ramps, have the potential to seriously injure you.

Flight line or ramp hazards vary in seriousness. They can be from small puncture wounds from safety wire to fatal injuries resulting from inattention to the surroundings, or failing to follow manufacturers established instructions and procedures...

Aviation Maintenance Technicians (AMT's) have an enormous responsibility for ensuring that all aircraft remain airworthy. This all begins with safety for you as the technician, for your co-workers, customers, and the equipment...
Safety prevention is inexpensive compared to the cost of an injury or death.
Let's begin our lesson on FLIGHT LINE SAFETY..............................
LESSON MENU
PERSONAL PROTECTION
DISCUSSION

The first line of defense against aviation hazards is Personal Protection. Life threatening, or life altering, hazards are inherent with the aviation industry and it is everyone's responsibility to maintain a safe workforce...

The AMT is offered numerous opportunities to protect themselves while in the workforce. This can be in the form of actual safety equipment that is worn on your body, to written safety literature from the regulatory authorities, commercial vendors, military, and employers...
Personal protection must be worn in order for it to keep you safe. It will not help you if it is stuck in a locker or toolbox. Let's start out with what we can do to protect our eyes.
You must always be cognizant of your eye safety. Safety glasses are your number one defense against eye injury.

There are many eye hazards that you need to be aware of. Here are just some of them: st, dirt, rocks, and foreign objects that are blown around by jet exhaust and propeller or rotor wash. * Aircraft system fluids that is accidentally spilled or sprayed. * Dropped tools from high levels. * Cut safety wire. * Power and pneumatic tool chips and shavings. * Sharp and pointed edges on the aircraft and engine.....

The big question to ask is why doesn't more people wear safety glasses? The answer seems to be because the majority of safety glasses made have a one size fit all mentality and they are uncomfortable...

It is very important that you find a pair that fits you properly, is comfortable to wear, and you feel they look good on you. Doing these three things will make wearing the safety glasses feel more normal, and in the long run, your eyes will thank you...
Another hazard that you need to be aware of concerns how you dress while performing maintenance on an aircraft.

In aviation, you will be required to remove all jewelry (rings, bracelets, watches, necklaces, etc.) prior to working on an aircraft. This is a practice that also should be carried over to your home life when working with machinery.

Many technicians have lost their fingers, had their arms or head pulled in rotating components, or was electrocuted when their ring or watch touched an electrical circuit. Don't take a chance. Remove your jewelry prior to working on any aircraft or machinery...
Long sleeve or baggy clothing has no place around machinery. Baggy clothing can be caught and wrapped around moving components or protruding objects;. and cause physical injuries.

Another area of concern is with the inherent noise that is produced by aircraft. There should be warning placards in any area where the noise level exceeds 94db. If a person cannot understand you from two feet away in a normal voice, there is a good chance that the noise level exceeds the 94db...
You should have hearing protection available anytime you are exposed to noise levels above the 94db. This can be in the form of earplugs, earmuffs, or a combination of the two.
Most individuals never realize they are losing their hearing until it is too late. Once you lose your hearing, it is gone for good. You should have your hearing protection with you at all times.

As in any industrial complex, safety shoes should be worn by all AMT's. When picking out a pair of steel or composite toed shoes, ensure that the soles are resilient to petroleum products such as fuels and lubricants. Spilled fluids occur on a daily basis and traction from your work shoes is very important...

Hard hats are not normally worn while working on aircraft. They should be worn however anytime heavy aircraft components are being lifted over your head with a hoist during the removal or installation process...
The chemicals in use today within the aviation industry can have long term affects on your health if inhaled into your lungs or absorbed through the skin.

Chemicals that evaporate quickly should be used with extreme caution. Special masks that can remove the chemical residue from the air must be worn when there is any doubt as to the safety precautions prescribed in the MSDS...
Use Latex gloves to protect your hands while working with chemicals.

FLIGHT LINE OPERATIONS
The AMT on the flight line will be exposed to numerous types of Ground Support Equipment, more commonly known as GSE.
DISCUSSION

Just as the name implies, this equipment is used to support aircraft while on the ground, and aircraft require a plethora of specialized equipment in order to perform its day-to-day operations. Let's look at some of the more common pieces of equipment that you will come in contact with...
The most common or universal piece of GSE is the tow tractor, or more commonly known as the tug or mule. It is used to tow aircraft and GSE on the flight line and in hangars.
Tow tractors are specialized pieces of GSE. The have powerful engines and have a gear reduction that allows them to pull heavy loads.
The tow tractors are categorized by the amount of weight they can pull, environmental conditions they will operate in, and by their turning radius.

It is very important that one not attempt to tow anything heavier than the tow tractor is rated for. Premature transmission failure and the reduced ability to stop the tow are two of the main reasons not to exceed the rated tow weight...
All motorized ground support is limited to a maximum speed of 15 mph on an open ramp, and 5 mph around aircraft.

The aircraft tow bar is used to connect the aircraft to the tow tractor. There are numerous types of tow bars with each one made specifically for a type of aircraft. The NT4 or universal tow bar can tow numerous types of aircraft up to 90,000 pounds...
Some aircraft will need a special piece of GSE to start the engines or run electrical systems. The most common types are the Air Starter or Puffer, and the power cart.

The air starter has a small jet engine that is attached to a trailer and enclosed in a metal box. The engine produces high volume and high pressure air that is transferred to the aircraft starting port by a hose...

Air starters are known to reach a noise level above 140db; so hearing protection is mandatory. fire extinguisher must be close to the piece of equipment in case of an emergency. * Never engage the air valve that allows the air to flow to the aircraft until the coupling on the aircraft is attached and secure and the pilot or maintenance personnel in the cockpit have given their permission. * The air starter should be left hooked up to the tow tractor in case on an emergency.....
A fire extinguisher must be close to the piece of equipment in case of an emergency.

Never engage the air valve that allows the air to flow to the aircraft until the coupling on the aircraft is attached and secure and the pilot or maintenance personnel in the cockpit have given their permission.
The air starter should be left hooked up to the tow tractor in case on an emergency.
The electrical power cart is used to provide electrical power to the aircraft. This reduces the risk of having a dead battery when electrical power is needed for engine starts or maintenance.

Electrical power carts have either diesel (more often) or gas (less often) engines that drives a large generator. They can provide both AC and DC power to the aircraft through 50-foot heavy cables. A special male adapter plug is inserted into the receptacle in the side of the airframe.....

Hydraulic test stands, more commonly known as the Hydraulic Jenny, provide hydraulic pressure to the aircraft's hydraulic system for accomplishing maintenance and tests. These units run at very high pressures and should only be used by qualified personnelll
The Air Conditioning unit provides cool air to the aircraft.
This is used strictly for comfort of the maintenance technicians performing maintenance inside of the aircraft and is more common in hotter climates..
Aircraft servicing vehicles come in numerous shapes, sizes, purposes, and configurations. The most common of these are the fuel, lubrication, and sanitation vehicles.

As the name applies, the fuel truck will either fuel or defuel the aircraft. Most fuel trucks are run through contractors that supply fuel to an airport. Some smaller airfields will require the AMT to drive the fuel truck to the aircraft...

Fuel trucks should always park perpendicular to the aircraft when fueling. This allows an emergency egress path for the truck in case of a fire. Fuel trucks are also limited to the 5 mph and 10 mph speed limits we spoke of earlier in this lesson..

Servicing trucks will normally contain the lubrications, air, and the different greases required on the aircraft. These include the engine oil, hydraulic fluids, and consumables such as rags and brushes..

There are numerous specialized tools that are designed for a specific aircraft that can be considered ground support equipment. Fixtures and tools to remove components from the aircraft, special jacking pads, and test equipment are just a few of the examples of these special tools...
The last piece of ground support equipment that we need to cover is the check stands. The check stand is used to work on areas too high to reach, or on areas that could be considered unstable...
Some check stands are manufactured to a set shape and size for performing major maintenance on the aircraft. Others are portable and adjustable in height and have wheels for mobility.

The AMT must always be on the look out for hidden dangers. The basic ingredient to aviation flight line and shop safety is good house keeping.
The Occupational, Health, and Safety Administration (OSHA) are the federal regulatory authority that sets the personal and industrial safety standards that the AMT must comply with.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) sets and enforces all aviation standards and regulations with regard to aircraft operations and movement within the United States.
Cleanliness of your workspace is very important. Tripping, slipping, cutting, etc., hazards are averted by picking up items and wiping up spills. Let's be a little more specific.

Chemicals present their own unique and hidden dangers. We are exposed to all types of chemicals on a daily basis. How do you know if the product is dangerous?

All employers are mandated to have a Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) for every chemical that is stored or used within the premises. Chemicals can be considered anything from fuel, oil, or grease, to the liquid hand soap that is by the sink...
The MSDS' contain a wealth of information on the health risks and proper use each chemical. To start with, ensure that you always wear latex gloves when handling all fuels and oils.
After cleanliness, comes your own personal safety. Proper lighting in your workplace will allow you to see exactly what you are doing. This includes inside the shop as well as on the flight line...

You should always inspect all tools and equipment before you use them. Here are some key areas to be aware of with compressed air and air tools: * Equipment and tools wear out. They do not last forever. * Air hoses are pulled across the work area and are chaffed through the protective covering. Worn hoses can blow apart and whip back and forth uncontrollably. * The quick disconnect fittings are dropped on the ground and damaged. This can cause the fittings to depart the hose without warning. * Dust and dirt become lodged in the end of hoses and exhaust ports on air tools. The material can be discharged at a high rate of speed. * Compressor tanks will corrode on the inside if the condensation is not drained daily. The corrosion or rust will be expelled out through the hose like a bullet, or sent through the tool and damage it. * Never aim compressed air at another person. * Never use compressed air to blow the dust off of tools or yourself...

Some of these ideas may appear to be common sense, but people are killed every year because of inattention.
Always approach and depart an operating aircraft within the vision of the pilot. NEVER approach or depart a rotary wing aircraft toward the tail rotor.
Rotating propellers, propeller wash, rotor blades, jet intakes and exhausts are just some of the reasons to be aware of the activity going on around you.

Safety glasses and hearing protection are required around all operating aircraft because of the danger of rocks and other debris being blown around and the high noise levels of aircraft flight lines...

Everyone should stay clear of the propeller and engine exhaust anytime a propeller driven aircraft is started. Personnel have become fixated upon a rotating propeller and accidentally walked right into the rotating blades to get the aircraft chocks...
Once a propeller driven aircraft is started, a powerful propeller wash is developed that can blow a person or unsecured GSE (Ground Support Equipment) around.

Jet engine aircraft pose their own unique dangers. A very strong suction is located at the intake of the engine. An unknowing person could be sucked right into an operating engine from 25 feet away and at up to 45 degrees from the engine inlet...
Because of this suction, you should not wear a hat or have any lose rags or objects on your person that could be sucked into the intake.

Jet exhaust is very hot and is considered dangerous up to 200 feet behind an operating engine. The temperature at 200 feet could be more than 100 degrees F. Needless to say, the high speed of the exhaust combined with any foreign objects on the ramp could become dangerous projectiles. Another reason for wearing safety glasses!!!!!!
Jet engines also produce a very high whine type noise. Decibel levels over 140db can be reached with most jet engines. This is another reason that hearing protection is mandatory.
